$comment: THE PRE-DECLARED PROBE TABLE for scripts/check-static-form-equivalence.mjs (ADR-15 kinds 1 and 2, #310).
WHAT `equivalence` MEANS HERE, STATED BEFORE THE TABLE RATHER THAN IMPLIED BY IT.
The `scenarios` x `observables` cross product below is a LIBRARY-ONLY bar: every outcome in it is
measured on a page whose only author CSS is this library's own. On that bar the generated static
form is required to be EQUAL to the shadow form, within one engine, and the gate fails on any
divergence. That is the whole of what this gate certifies, and it is deliberately less than the
phrase `equal to the shadow form` sounds like.
WHAT IT DOES NOT CERTIFY, MEASURED RATHER THAN CONCEDED: `consumerOverrides` below. `:host`
declarations sit in the INNER tree, so a document declaration beats them at any weight and in any
order. Moved onto `.sk-<name>-host` they become ordinary (0,1,0) document declarations a consumer
must outbid. The wrapper therefore reproduces `:host`'s LAYOUT and HARDENS its cascade position —
#375, found by ADR-16's group H. Those rows are pinned by VERDICT (`diverge` or `equal`), never by
equality, because equality is not what CSS provides there. A gate that only ran the library-only
table would certify an equivalence it never tested; a gate that demanded equality on these rows
would demand something no document selector can give.
COMPARE WITHIN ONE ENGINE. ADR-15's 52 declared outcomes reach the same verdict in chromium and
firefox but not always the same VALUE: sk-action-row's grid tracks resolve from font metrics and
differ sub-pixel between engines for the same PASSING comparison. Nothing in this file is a
transcribed computed value for that reason. `consumerOverrides[].shadowValue` is the one exception
and every one of them is a keyword, never a length.
FLOORS ARE SHRINK-ONLY, the same shape expected-parts.json and check-adopted-css-boundaries.mjs's
own probe table use. Raise them when you add rows; lower one only with a reason in the commit
message. A green line over zero compared components is the vacuous pass this repository has
red-ed for twice, and `floors.components` is what refuses it.

$comment: #375's table, generalised from ADR-16 group H's four rows to every component this gate covers.
`staticWeight` is stated RELATIVE TO THE WRAPPER RULE, not relative to the shadow-side spelling,
and that asymmetry is the finding rather than a modelling convenience. In the shadow form a
consumer targets the custom element, which is a TYPE selector at (0,0,1). There is no document
spelling of the wrapper below (0,1,0), because the wrapper is reached by a class. So a consumer
who beat `:host` with `sk-action-row { … }` has to climb a whole specificity level merely to TIE
`.sk-action-row-host`, and even the tie loses unless their sheet is later.
`against` names the EMITTED rule each row competes with, and the gate reads that rule out of the generated
sheet, asserts it declares the property in question, and computes the boundary from it. The boundary is
never a constant: `position: sticky` on sk-page-header is emitted by a MODIFIER rule at (0,2,0) while
`display` on the same component is emitted by the base wrapper rule at (0,1,0).
`below` rows diverge. `tie` rows diverge when the consumer's rule is authored FIRST and are equal
when it is authored LAST — a bundler's decision more often than a consumer's. `above` rows are
equal in either order. Those three lines ARE the ruled limit: not `the wrapper always wins`, but
`strictly outbid it, or be later`.
`verdict` is pinned; the computed values are recorded but not pinned, except `shadowValue`, which
is a keyword in every row that has one. A row flipping from `diverge` to `equal` is a FAILURE
here, not an improvement: it would mean the emitted wrapper's weight changed under everyone who
has already written an override against it, and that is a decision, not a side effect.

rows.note: ADR-16 H1/H2. The identical intent at (0,0,1) wins against the element and loses against the wrapper, in either order.
ADR-16 H3/H4, the sharper pair — a consumer can switch the ELEMENT's container off from the document at (0,0,1), and cannot switch the wrapper's off at a (0,1,0) tie authored first.
the same override read one level down: destroying the element's container stops @container (max-width: 400px) firing, and the wrapper's survives.
THE TIE, resolved by ORDER. The same equal-weight override authored AFTER the sheet wins in both forms.
STRICTLY OUTBID at (0,2,0), authored first — equal in both forms. This row with H2 is what makes the boundary a number rather than a warning.
#375's `plus the sk-app-shell equivalents`, on the kind-1 exemplar.

the container-destroying override read at the rule the presentation axis actually drives. `shadowValue` is a LENGTH here and is deliberately unpinned — see this file's $comment on within-engine comparison.
the component ADR-15 ruled on without measuring.
the container-destroying override on the unmeasured component, at the tie.

the BARE host-attribute axis, overridden. A consumer switching sticky off from the document succeeds against the element and fails against the wrapper — the axis whose subject IS the host is where this matters most.

the same intent spelled at the weight of the rule ACTUALLY EMITTING `position`, authored LAST — equal. Note which selector that is: `position: sticky` is declared by the MODIFIER rule at (0,2,0), not by the base wrapper rule at (0,1,0). The boundary is a property of the rule you are overriding, never a constant, which is why `against` names it and the gate reads the weight off the generated sheet.

floors.$comment: `engines` is 1 rather than 2 because WebKit cannot launch on the maintainer workstation (ADR-10's recorded host gap) and firefox is not installed in every job. The gate names every engine it ran and every engine it could not, and refuses to run on none.
